images.caption: Figure 1:Scientific principle construction as a bottleneck in scientific discovery.As experimental observations accumulate, researchers formulate tentative explanations of individual outcomes, generalize recurring relationships across observations into scientific principles, and reassess these explanations in light of new observations. The resulting principles guide further investigation, forming an iterative discovery cycle. However, this process requires substantial domain expertise, time, labor, and financial resources, limiting the pace of scientific discovery.

Figure 2:Overview ofPrincipia.Given scientific inputs and their observed outcomes,Principiaforms comparative causal hypotheses that explain how input characteristics may contribute to the outcomes. It groups related inputs through similarity-based clustering and inductively generalizes their associated hypotheses into scientific principles. Retrieved hypotheses and principles guide subsequent prediction or candidate generation. New observations are then used to revise the hypotheses involved, and the updated hypotheses support principle reconstruction, forming a continuous cycle of scientific knowledge construction and application.
